cards.text: Jesus just stood at Lazarus's tomb in Bethany and called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” And the man who had been dead walked out, still wrapped in strips of linen. A crowd of people who came to Mary saw the WHOLE thing.

cards.question: Many of the people who came to Mary and saw Lazarus walk out believe in Jesus.

cards.text: But some of them go to the Pharisees, a group of strict religious leaders, and tell them what Jesus had done. A dead man just WALKED OUT of a tomb, friend. That news was NEVER staying in Bethany.

cards.question: The chief priests and the Pharisees call their council, the Sanhedrin, together and ask, “What are we to do?” What do they say Jesus is doing?
The council says if they let Jesus go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and then the ___ will come and take away their place and their nation.

cards.text: Then Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, speaks up, and his opening line to the council is “You know nothing at all!” WHOA, friend, I've had gentler wake-ups from a smoke alarm.

cards.question: Caiaphas tells the council it's better for them that one man ___ for the people than that the whole nation perish.

cards.text: Now the Gospel pauses the meeting for a quick word about what Caiaphas just said.

cards.question: Caiaphas said those words about one man dying for the people on his own.

cards.text: As high priest that year, Caiaphas was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation, and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God. I bet that man had NO idea what he just said.

cards.question: Jesus would die for the nation and for the scattered children of God. What would that do for the scattered children of God?

answers.text: Make them priests in the temple
Set them free from the Romans

cards.question: After Caiaphas speaks, from that day on, the council plots to ___ Jesus.

cards.text: As a result, Jesus no longer goes about publicly among the Jews. He withdraws to a town in an area near the wilderness and stays there with the disciples.

cards.question: Jesus and the disciples stay in a town in an area near the wilderness. What's the town called?

cards.text: Meanwhile the Jewish Passover is near, and many people go up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the feast. That's RUSH HOUR, friend. Everybody headed the same direction, all at once.

cards.question: Standing in the temple courts before Passover, the crowds are all sure Jesus will come to the feast.
While the crowds wonder about Jesus, the chief priests and Pharisees have given orders about Him. What are the orders?

answers.text: Anyone who knows where He is must report it
Anyone who follows Him must leave the city
No one may say His name in the temple

findings.problem: Card 8 tells nothing from the passage. It only says the Gospel is about to comment on Caiaphas's words. John 11:51 is retold on card 10, so card 8 is a filler transition that cites a verse it doesn't tell.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Card 8 is one flat, stripped-down sentence with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a narrator's stage direction, not Papa Dorin telling the story.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The purpose of the orders in John 11:57, 'so that they could arrest Him,' is never told on any card. This is the passage's closing beat. The walkthrough ends on the order to report and leaves out where the plot is headed.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
